title: How to Run AI on Your Own Laptop

scenes.text: Run AI free, on your laptop. What if you could chat with an AI, with no internet, no subscription, and nothing leaving your computer? [1] You can, today, on a normal laptop. [2] Let's see how to run AI locally.

It takes three simple steps. [1] Install a tool, like Ollama, or LM Studio. [2] Download an open model, like Llama, Qwen, or Gemma, often a 4 bit version. [3] Start chatting. Everything runs on your own machine.

[1] What can your laptop handle? [2] With 8 gigabytes of RAM, try small models, around 3 billion parameters. [3] With 16 gigabytes, 7 to 8 billion parameter models run nicely. [4] With 32 gigabytes or more, you can try models around 30 billion parameters, at 4 bits.

Why run locally? [1] Privacy, your data never leaves your laptop. No monthly fees. It works offline, on a plane, or in a village. [2] But it's slower than the cloud, the models are smaller, and it uses your battery.

What do people use local AI for? [1] Summarising private documents, like contracts or medical reports. [2] Coding help, without sharing company code. [3] And learning, experimenting with different models for free.

Here are four terms. [1] Local inference, running a model on your own device. [2] Tokens per second, how fast it writes. [3] Context length, how much text it can read at once. [4] And a local server, which lets your own apps talk to the model, like an API.

Here's a common myth. [1] People think you need an expensive gaming PC to run AI. [2] Small models run on everyday laptops. Apple's M series chips, with shared memory, handle them especially well. A GPU helps, but isn't required.

data.myth: You need an expensive gaming PC to run AI.
data.fact: Small models run on everyday laptops. A GPU helps, but isn't required.
